description: I am Kushagra Singh Adhikari, a solo participant representing Code0. My project, ASTRA-MED, aims to monitor astronaut health, track vital signs, identify potential risks, and provide explainable alerts. By combining AI, software development, and credible NASA research, I hope to support astronaut well-being and contribute to safer, healthier space exploration.
summary:
ASTRAMED is an astronaut health monitoring and research platform developed to support safer and better-informed human space exploration. Spaceflight exposes astronauts to health challenges such as muscle deconditioning, cardiovascular changes, sleep disruption, isolation, and radiation exposure.

The platform brings together crew health information, health trends, YOMA (a camera-based movement assessment tool), and scientific research from NASA’s Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) and Europe PMC. It helps users explore health-related information, understand changes over time, and connect scientific research with the challenges of human spaceflight.

ASTRAMED clearly separates actual measurements, synthetic demonstration data, and published research to maintain data transparency. Its goal is to make astronaut health information more accessible and understandable, supporting research and better-informed decisions for future space missions.
details:
About ASTRAMED

ASTRAMED is an astronaut health monitoring and research platform designed to support safer human space exploration. It brings together crew health information, health trends, camera-based movement assessment, and scientific research in one interactive platform.

How Does It Work?

ASTRAMED provides several connected modules:

- Mission Overview: Gives users a central view of mission-related health information.
- Crew & Body Monitor: Organizes astronaut profiles and available health information through an interactive interface and 3D body visualization.
- Health Trends: Helps users explore changes in available health measurements over time.
- YOMA: Explores camera-based movement assessment using visible body movements and pose estimation. It is intended to support movement analysis, not measure internal vital signs.
- AI Assistant – Mrs. Space: Provides contextual guidance, explains platform features, and helps users understand health information and research.
- NASA Research Library: Integrates research from NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) and Europe PMC, helping users explore scientific studies relevant to human spaceflight.

The platform also includes a clearly labelled Demo Mode with fictional astronaut profiles and synthetic readings for demonstration purposes.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRAMED aims to make astronaut health information easier to access, organize, and understand. It brings monitoring, movement assessment, health trends, and scientific research into one interface. This could help researchers, students, and future mission-support teams explore health-related information and identify areas that need further investigation.

Technology and Tools Used

The project was developed using React, TypeScript, JavaScript, and Node.js, with a web-based interface and backend. It uses camera-based pose estimation concepts for YOMA, 3D visualization for body interaction, GitHub for source-code management, and Render for deployment and public hosting. NASA OSDR and Europe PMC provide access to relevant scientific research.

Creativity and Design Considerations

ASTRAMED combines multiple space-health-related functions into one mission-support platform rather than treating them as separate tools. Its dark, futuristic mission-control interface is designed to make complex information easier to navigate. During development, we considered scientific accuracy, usability, accessibility, limited computing resources, data transparency, and the distinction between real measurements, synthetic demonstration data, and published research.

ASTRAMED is a prototype intended to explore how technology and scientific research can support future astronaut health monitoring. It is not a certified medical system and does not diagnose medical conditions or replace validated medical sensors.
